hook.text: Hervé This and Nicholas Kurti coined 'molecular gastronomy' in 1988—applying physics and chemistry to cooking.

buildup.text: Molecular gastronomy uses science to understand why recipes work: why soufflés rise, why steaks brown, why emulsions break.

discovery.text: Ferran Adrià at elBulli turned science into art—spherified olives, frozen parmesan air, and transparent ravioli made from gelling.

twist.text: Most molecular gastronomy techniques (gelling, emulsifying, foaming) were used in industrial food processing for decades.

climax.text: elBulli served 50 diners per night with a staff of 50—half the team was R&D. It closed in 2011, but molecular gastronomy's.

punchline.text: Science meets kitchen. Industrial techniques become art.

quiz.question: Where did most molecular gastronomy techniques originally come from?
options: Industrial food processing used them for decades—chefs borrowed from factories
